pr_title: Fix occasional non-fatal errors from polling API requests incorrectly getting queued twice
pr_body:
The cause was `Poll` getting called twice from two threads, in such a way that the same request was incorrectly queued twice to `APIAccess`.

I've fixed this at two levels. Rationale being that ensuring it runs on the update thread will potentially save future mistakes.

Closes #16672.

issue_context.title: Error occurred while handling an API request (loading multiplayer lobbies)
issue_context.body:
```csharp 2022-01-27 22:37:14 [error]: Error occurred while handling an API request. 2022-01-27 22:37:14 [error]: System.InvalidOperationException: The WebRequest has already been run. 2022-01-27 22:37:14 [error]: at osu.Framework.IO.Network.WebRequest.PerformAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) 2022-01-27 22:37:14 [error]: at osu.Framework.Extensions.ExceptionExtensions.ExceptionExtensions.Rethrow(Exception exception) 2022-01-27 22:37:14 [error]: at osu.Framework.Extensions.ExceptionExtensions.ExceptionExtensions.RethrowAsSingular(AggregateException aggregateException) 2022-01-27 22:37:14 [error]: at osu.Framework.IO.Network.WebRequest.Perform() 2022-01-27 22:37:14 [error]: at osu.Game.Online.API.APIRequest.Perform(IAPIProvider api) 2022-01-27 22:37:14 [error]: at osu.Game.Online.API.APIAccess.handleRequest(APIRequest req) ``` Very dodge. ### Discussed in https://github.com/ppy/osu/discussions/16667
Originally posted by **Theighlin** January 28, 2022 I went to the multiplayer lobby listing and this error popped up in the notifications. [runtime.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/7954264/runtime.log) [network.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/7954265/network.log)

review_comments: Is there a reason for these changes? Or are they just something that you've done along the way because why not? As far as I can tell they should not have any difference, right?

Does the commit message explain enough?

![20220128 161028 (Safari)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/151503149-8ab624a5-25a6-4977-9456-601a55673f8b.png)

Was just double-safety.

Can you explain how it's more safe? I just want to know what I'm missing for future implementations, because as it stands I would do it exactly the same way it was done previously.

In-fact isn't this technically more unsafe? If we're talking about the % chance that `lastPollRequest` is cancelled if this method is called asynchronously, then this has a lower % chance to cancel the request and a higher % chance to fire duplicates.

Again I'm just trying to know the thought process.

Because it was referencing a field, this caused it to be thread unsafe. Consider two threads running the method:

- Thread1 constructs a request
- Thread2 constructs a request (and overwrites the first)
- Thread1 queues the request
- Thread2 queues the request <- point of failure
Right, I see. So the problem is enqueueing the same request object in both paths. Okay.
